sources.title: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition, Hydrogen section
sources.extraction: pdfseparate -f 79 -l 79; one original PDF page, without OCR or changes to the contents. Whole-source PDF downloaded for review only.
sources.inspection: Page rendered at high resolution and visually inspected; the original scan has no usable embedded text. Sampled rows transcribed in printed_ph2_nodes.json.
sources.interpretation: The energy is an estimate based on assigning PH2 63 percent of the PH3 dissociation energy. Geometry and vibration inputs were estimated by analogy with PH3; this is not a modern measured partition function. The published uncertainty is not supplied with a probability convention. Online and printed formation columns differ, while the sampled molecular thermal columns agree.

sources.title: Revised Thermochemical Properties of Phosphinidene (PH), Phosphine (PH3), Phosphorus Nitride (PN), and Magnesium Phosphate (Mg3P2O8)
sources.journal: Journal of Physical and Chemical Reference Data 28, 1705-1712 (1999)
sources.inspection: Official NIST-hosted complete PDF downloaded; introduction p1705, Table2 p1706 and reference conversion discussion p1710 read. PDF not vendored.
sources.short_quote: only PH2(g) has a corrected table in the 4th edition of the NIST-JANAF Tables.

facts.reference_change: JANAF third edition changed the phosphorus reference from red-V to white phosphorus; five compounds initially escaped the change. PH2 was corrected in the printed fourth edition.

P_reference_ranges_K.P2_gas: Above 1180.008 K; half a mole P2 per mole P atoms.

limitations: The paper documents the printed-table correction, not the mechanism behind current online H-079 formation columns.
Online 125.938 minus printed 108.499 is 17.439 kJ/mol; do not silently replace that observed difference with Lodders rounded/contemporary 17.460 correction.
A reference change must be applied consistently to the atoms and molecules of a balanced reaction.

sources.title: NASA Glenn Coefficients for Calculating Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Species
sources.inspection: Official PDF Appendix D text inspected: PH2 printed p169, P p166, H p126. Selected records extracted with each line stripped of leading/trailing layout whitespace. Coefficients retained as printed.
limitations: The source authenticates the selected polynomial; it is not an independent measurement beyond its source compilation.
The original Gurvich pages were not recovered, so its experimental selection and reference conversion cannot be reconstructed here.
The stated polynomial interval does not establish physical accuracy throughout200-6000 K.

sources.title: NIST CCCBDB experimental data for PH2 (Phosphino radical)
sources.inspection: Official neutral-species HTML read, including identity, state, thermal table, geometry and bibliography.

facts.thermochemical_reference: Gurvich, Veyts, Alcock, Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Substances, Fourth Edition,1989.

limitations: This shares Gurvich ancestry with NASA; agreement is not independent corroboration.
Uncertainty convention and white/red reference state are not explicitly specified in this page.
The page attaches a silicon-cluster paper to a PH2 bending frequency; use the PH2 primary spectroscopy instead of that suspect citation.

sources.inspection: Complete author database mirror downloaded; PH2 commentary at line 32539 and four-line record starting 32545 directly inspected. Snapshot header last additions 3 January 2023, PH2 record A 5/05.
limitations: The selection is G3B3, not a copy of Gurvich. The cited alternatives are not additional measurements in this record.
White versus red-V phosphorus for the selected calculation is not explicit in the inspected PH2 record; atomic references and thermal model need review before adoption.
The meanings of listed vibrational frequencies and the full high-temperature electronic treatment are not derived by the comment alone.

sources.inspection: Supplied publisher correction PDF fully inspected and its PH2 row and footnotes visually checked. No change to the transcribed numerical values. The 2007 publisher abstract/SI description were inspected earlier; main/SI numerical content remains unavailable.

facts.method: CCSD(T) with complete-basis extrapolation, core-valence and scalar-relativistic corrections and scaled zero-point energies.

limitations: Correction concerns nitrogen entries; count the 2007 and 2009 versions as one theoretical source.

The original experimental cycle is not inspected. Reference-state identity for these numbers is not established from the accessible table; do not compare them as fully harmonized atomization energies.
The one-page correction does not identify white versus red-V phosphorus, or provide the atomization/ZPE/thermal-correction inputs needed for a common-reference reconstruction.

sources.title: A photoionization study of PH: PH2 revisited
sources.inspection: Publisher-registered Crossref abstract and bibliography retrieved; full paper not obtained.

facts.experiment: Photoionization of PH2 produced by H+PH3; comparison with earlier benzylphosphine pyrolysis results.
facts.caution: The approximately 0.70 eV splitting in the abstract is between PH2+ cation states; it is not the neutral PH2 electronic gap.

limitations: The33.1±0.6kcal/mol formation value is verified as quoted by Matus, not rederived from this experiment.
The original atom/PH3 anchors, white/red phosphorus reference and statistical interpretation of the uncertainty remain unverified.

sources.title: Heats of formation of phosphorus compounds determined by current methods of computational quantum chemistry
sources.inspection: Publisher-registered Crossref abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; original full paper not obtained.

facts.method: Restricted-reference CCSD(T)/CBS atomization with core-valence, relativistic and core-valence basis-set-superposition corrections; B3LYP geometries/frequencies.

sources.title: A dispersed fluorescence and ab initio investigation of the X2B1 and A2A1 electronic states of the PH2 molecule
sources.inspection: Author-hosted full PDF parsed through web tool; introduction,Tables II and III, and discussion read. Local download HTTP403; no byte hash available.

facts.geometry_method: CCSD(T)/cc-pV5Z frozen core; calculated, not a measured structure.

limitations: Provides measured vibronic levels and a coupled-state model, not a full validated 1500-4000 K thermodynamic table.
Measured fundamentals cannot be inserted as harmonic frequencies without specifying the anharmonic/rovibronic treatment.
The neutral A-X gap is distinct from PH2+ cation splittings.

sources.inspection: Official listing identifies 3286 species and version 1.172 (as of 2024-09-01). Searches within retrieved listing for PH2, H2P, and Phosph returned no matching text. Direct local fetch HTTP403.
sources.conclusion: No PH2 anchor identified in this version; no ATcT PH2 energy adopted.
limitations: This is a scoped negative lookup, not proof of absence from every ATcT version or unpublished network.
The ATcT citation in Matus table footnote l applies to NH3, not PH2.

correlations_and_reference_states: NASA 2002 and CCCBDB quote the same Gurvich 1989 evaluation; their agreement cannot be counted as two independent energy determinations.

Current JANAF online and printed fourth-edition values are not interchangeable. Lodders verifies historical red-V to white-P correction in the printed PH2 table. Online formation columns require a separate numerical integrity audit.

The modern theory values and Matus quoted experiment are promising leads. Their white/red elemental anchors have not been established here; no unqualified numerical ranking against NASA or printed JANAF is justified.
Matus 2007 and its2009 correction are one study. Burcat references to Ricca and Haworth are quotations rather than new independent data.
Any replacement must compare the balanced P(g)+2H(g)->PH2(g) reaction using compatible atomic and molecular anchors, not isolated formation enthalpies from unidentified phosphorus gauges.
No covariance information is available for the inspected non-ATcT values; quoted error bars are not combined into a synthetic uncertainty.

recommendation.runtime_action: Retain the current curated PH2 value for this investigation PR; mark the species inherited and unresolved, not validated.
recommendation.reason: The old JANAF estimate has weak energy/thermal support, but online-versus-print reference issues, missing original Gurvich details, and unharmonized modern atomization anchors prevent certification of a replacement. NASA is useful as a controlled alternative, not established scientific truth.
recommendation.scientific_priority: Audit the modern CCSD(T)/CBS and photoionization evidence and its atomic/white-P references before choosing an energy. Combine a selected balanced energy with a separately justified thermal model informed by PH2 spectroscopy.
required_before_adoption: Recover and evaluate the original Berkowitz thermochemical cycle and the Ricca/Haworth/Matus atomic-reference details.
Harmonize white-P/red-V, 0 K/298 K, and P/H atomic formation references.
Audit a full temperature-dependent model, including anharmonic vibration and neutral excited-state treatment, over the actual target interval.
Repeat controlled finite equilibrium perturbations and retain a legacy dataset if a later default change is justified.
recommendation.interpretation_of_current_provenance: Numerical closeness of the current FastChem PH2 fit to the printed corrected JANAF family can clarify its origin; it does not independently validate the1963 estimated physical energy.

search_limitations: Original Berkowitz 1989, Ricca 1998, Haworth 2002 full texts not recovered; access status distinguishes direct evidence from subsequent quotations.

The Matus 2009 correction is now locally supplied and visually inspected; the 2007 main/SI and experimental 1989 paper remain uninspected. The Jakubek 2006 author PDF was readable through the web tool but not locally downloaded.
No exhaustive survey of all post-2009 PH2 energetics or all ATcT versions is claimed.
Solid high-pressure PH2 phases and ligand fragments named PH2 are outside the neutral gas-radical scope.
